about: A dreamlike cave adventure. An old silver-haired man says you must prove yourself worthy. You explore dim underground lands and meet a hooded double who shadows you.

done.why: The hooded-figure encounter resolved in a way I liked, and I stopped at a crawlway junction. I had not found a goal.

moments.note: Turning the lantern off and on again made the hooded figure appear and put a glowing sword in my hand.
The beaten figure lowered its head and waited. Removing its hood showed my own face, which then aged.
Footsteps that wait when you hold your breath.
The lantern is called a lamp, although I had called it a lantern.

wished: Talk to the footsteps or the mist.
Pull the sword from the rock at the junction.

lines.line: You slowly remove the hood from your badly wounded opponent and recoil in horror at the sight of your own face, weary and wounded.
lines.why: The scene's turning point. It ends the fight by showing you yourself.

lines.line: Quiet. Then, perhaps, footsteps; then quiet again. They are keeping your pace, and when you hold your breath to hear them better, they wait too.

fun.why: Short, and the surprise encounter paid off.

engagement.why: The footsteps drew me on, and the fight gave a clear moment to act in.

difficulty.why: The fight was gentle and the way ahead was clear.

interestingness.why: A double who mirrors you is a strong idea.
